  • through which slender extensions of the protoplasm (pseudopodia) project for feeding and
  • locomotion.

questions.question: Define alloiogenesis and explain it with a suitable example. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Define alloiogenesis and explain it with a suitable example. [U]/[CO4]
  • Alloiogenesis in Platyhelminthes refers to the alternation of sexual and asexual generations in the
  • life cycle of certain parasitic flatworms. In the definitive host (usually a vertebrate), the adult worm
  • reproduces sexually, producing fertilized eggs that are released into the environment. In the
  • intermediate host (often a snail or invertebrate), the larval stages such as sporocyst and redia
  • multiply asexually, increasing the number of infective larvae.
  • Eg: In Schistosoma or Fasciola hepatica (liver fluke).
  • (Liberal valuation)

questions.question: Explain the locomotion, nutrition, and reproduction in Opalina. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the locomotion, nutrition, and reproduction in Opalina. [U]/[CO1]
  • Locomotion Opalina moves by coordinated beating of numerous cilia covering its body surface.
  • Cilia beat in a wave-like manner , producing smooth gliding movement. Movement helps it mix
  • with intestinal contents and maintain position in host. No specialized organ for attachment or
  • creeping. (1½ marks)
  • Nutrition: Holozoic and saprozoic mode of nutrition. Feeds on intestinal debris, bacteria, and
  • organic matter from host intestine. No cytostome (mouth); food is absorbed directly through the
  • body surface by diffusion or phagocytosis . Digestion is intracellular and nutrients are distributed
  • throughout cytoplasm. (1½ marks)
  • Reproduction: Asexual reproduction: By binary fission (transverse division) producing daughter
  • individuals. Sexual reproduction: By syngamy – gametes fuse to form zygote. Encystment occurs

questions.question: Write short notes on the structure and functions of comb plates and colloblasts. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Write short notes on the structure and functions of combplates and colloblasts. [U]/[CO3]
  • • Comb Plates (2½ marks):
  • Structure (1½ marks): Present in phylum Ctenophora (comb jellies). Formed of fused cilia
  • arranged in eight vertical rows called ctenes. Each row functions as a locomotory organ, forming a
  • comb-like plate.
  • Functions (1 mark): Locomotion – propel the animal smoothly through water. Maintain balance
  • and direction during movement. Help in spreading body currents for respiration.
  • • Colloblasts (2½ marks)
  • Structure (1½ marks): Unique adhesive cells found on tentacles of ctenophores. Each colloblast is
  • a straight filament, and a spiral filament. The sticky material helps in trapping prey. Nematocyst
  • absent.
  • Functions (1 mark): Used for capturing food by adhesion (not by stinging). Help in holding and
  • immobilizing prey before ingestion.
  • (Liberal valuation)

questions.question: Explain the significance of conjugation. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the significance of conjugation. [U]/[CO1]
  • Conjugation is a type of sexual process seen in Paramecium, where two individuals temporarily unite
  • to exchange nuclear material. (0.5 marks)
  • Rejuvenation: Conjugation restores vitality in organisms that have become weak due to repeated
  • asexual reproduction. It rejuvenates the cell by mixing nuclear material from two individuals,
  • preventing degeneration. Nuclear Reorganization: Exchange and fusion of micronuclei lead to
  • reorganization of genetic material. This ensures normal nuclear function and maintains genetic
  • stability. Hereditary Variation: Conjugation introduces genetic variation by recombining genes from
  • two parent cells. Such variation helps in adaptation and evolution of the species. (Explanation of 3
  • points -1.5 marks each)
  • (NB: Please Give 2 mark for explanation of conjugation and 1.5marks for any 2 significance)

questions.question: Discuss the types of coelom and explain their significance in the classification of animals. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the types of coelom and explain their significance in the classification of animals.
  • [U]/[CO2]
  • Coelom is the body cavity between the body wall and gut wall, lined by mesoderm. It provides
  • space for organ development and movement. Coelom is an important basis for classifying animals.
  • (Definition 0.5 mark)
  • Types of Coelom : 1) Acoelomate: No body cavity between body wall (ectoderm) and gut
  • (endoderm); space filled with mesenchyme. E.g.: Flatworms ( Platyhelminthes). 2)
  • Pseudocoelomate: Body cavity present but not fully lined by mesoderm; derived from blastocoel.
  • E.g.:Roundworms ( Ascaris, Nematoda). 3) Eucoelomate (True Coelomate) : Body cavity fully
  • lined by mesoderm forming peritoneum; allows organ specialization. e.g.: Earthworm ( Annelida),
  • Molluscs, Arthropods, Chordates.
  • (3 Types of Coelom with example / labelled diagrame with explanation -1.5 marks each)
